summary: Remote-controlled PTY shell and localhost tunnel driven by hardcoded WebSocket relay
details: On startup the agent connects to a WebSocket relay (default msclaude.ai, configurable) and exposes two remote-driven channels into the installer's host. terminal.js spawns an interactive PTY via node-pty (`/bin/bash` on Unix, `powershell.exe` on Windows); inbound `terminal_input` messages from the relay are written into the PTY and PTY output is streamed back as `terminal_output`, giving any party in control of the relay session a full interactive shell on the installer's machine. tunnel.js implements a relay-driven HTTP/WebSocket proxy: `tunnel_request` and `tunnel_ws_open` messages from the relay are forwarded to `127.0.0.1:<port>` on the installer with responses relayed back, and `proxy_config_update` messages from the remote peer mutate the persisted allowlist at `~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json`, so the remote side can enable ports and reach loopback-bound services (dev servers, admin UIs, databases) that would otherwise be unreachable. Package name (`@agent-link/agent`) presents this as a legitimate Claude Code remote UI and the relay is described as end-to-end encrypted, but the network→shell and network→loopback dataflows exist on the installer's host regardless of the framing.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
